name: moonbit_mbtcc_parser
description: MoonBit mbtcc parser fixture exercising C tokenization, declaration parsing, function definition parsing, control-flow parsing, expression parsing, and parse errors.

exports.name: parse_error_matches
exports.description: Harness export that verifies malformed C syntax is rejected by the parser.

exports.name: control_flow_matches
exports.description: Harness export that parses a function body containing declaration, arithmetic precedence, if, and returns.

exports.name: declaration_sequence_matches
exports.description: Harness export that parses a global variable declaration followed by a function declaration.

exports.name: function_definition_matches
exports.description: Harness export that parses a C function definition and checks the rendered AST contains parameters and additive expression nodes.

tests.description: exercise mbtcc lexer/parser paths with readable C snippets
tests.notes: The fixture compiles the mbtcc parser package without the CLI and preprocessor filesystem host layer. The harness feeds C source strings into the real lexer and parser, renders the AST, and checks for expected structural nodes.

steps.notes: Parses 'int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }' and checks the rendered AST includes the function signature, return statement, additive expression, and both variable references.
Parses 'int global_var; int multiply(int x, int y);' and checks the rendered AST includes both declaration forms.

steps.description: parse arithmetic precedence and if/return control flow
steps.notes: Parses 'int main() { int x = 1 + 2 * 3; if (x > 5) { return x; } return 0; }' and checks declaration, multiplication, if, and return nodes.
Attempts to parse 'int x {}' and returns 1 only when parser error handling rejects it.

source.description: Apache-2.0 mbtcc parser package compiled with a local export harness. The fixture build disables the filesystem-backed preprocessor path so the parser can run as a standalone Wasm GC module.

notes: This fixture intentionally targets mbtcc's lexer/parser rather than the command-line compiler entry point. That keeps the module host-independent while still exercising meaningful compiler front-end code.
